items.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021
items.q: Miles makes it mysterious. Wayne Shorter makes it mysterious.

ctx.x: Yeah. Congratulations on the recording and — we’re approaching about an hour. I have just a couple more things I want to ask you. Two questions about playing with other people. Have you ever had an experience, like you talk about Rich Perry, and he’ll play who Rich Perry is. Have you ever had to ask a horn player or someone in your trio or quartet to play differently?

I think not so much professionally. I used to have a thing with bass players about playing on top of the beat or something, which I’m not, I mean that’s not the way I think of it now. But sometimes if somebody was dragging I’d want them to liven it up a little bit. So that was more of a general thing. I think what I told some student saxophone players, especially ones who are terrific technicians and have a lot of chops, it’s like you know put some mystery into it. Like I’m not getting you know, at Eastman, one…
Excellent. You anticipated one of my questions and it was about bass players. So I’m going to just wrap up with you know you were at Eastman for eleven plus years and —
